result.title: PRIME: Predictive Routing of Interventions by Modeling Effects for Scientific Ideation
result.summary: Feedback-driven iteration is widely used to improve LLM-generated scientific ideas, but existing systems either leave revision decisions implicit in generation, align revisions with feedback-localized weaknesses, or restrict action selection to system-specific operations. This is problematic because problems, hypotheses, and solutions are interdependent: the location where a weakness manifests does not itself determine the revision scope that will produce a better successor. We term this phenomenon diagnosis-intervention mismatch. We introduce Predictive Routing of Interventions by Modeling Effects (PRIME), a plug-and-play feedback-to-revision decision layer for existing scientific ideators. PRIME operates in three stages: (1) Structural Attribution interprets feedback over the problem-hypothesis-solution structure without fixing a revision target; (2) Counterfactual Routing constructs alternative scope-conditioned interventions and compares their projected successor utility and risks through lightweight rollouts; and (3) Intervention Execution compiles the selected intervention into an ordered generator-facing plan with semantic actions, preservation constraints, and dependency requirements for successor generation. We validate diagnosis intervention mismatch on 112 human-annotated idea-feedback pairs. Across four benchmarks, two ideators, and fixed- and open-problem settings, PRIME improves successor quality and routing reliability over strong baselines; removing counterfactual routing reduces quality from 3.463 to 1.960 and increases route regret from 0.426 to 1.929, confirming cross-scope effect modeling as the primary source of its gains.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出 LLM 科学想法迭代中存在「诊断—干预错配」，即弱点显现位置并不决定有效的修订范围，并提出 PRIME 决策层：结构化归因反馈、用轻量 rollout 比较不同范围的候选干预效用与风险，再编译为具体修订计划。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽面向文本科学想法而非多模态推理，但其「症状位置≠干预范围」的问题表述与用 rollout 预估后继效用来选择干预的做法，可能为 LVR 中确定 latent 更新范围与视觉证据筛选提供类比线索，可供核查。
